questions.q: What is a patch in TimesFM?
options: A group of consecutive values treated as one input unit
why: A patch is not tied to the period.

questions.q: A context of 960 values is split into patches of 32. How many tokens?
Attention cost grows with the square of the number of tokens. Going from 480 point-tokens to 15 patch-tokens (patch length 32) makes the attention part about how many times cheaper?
Which is a good test of a claim that a foundation model is better?
options: Compare to seasonal naive, ETS and a tuned GBM on a rolling-origin backtest, on data after the pretraining period
why: A random forecast is a trivial bar.
Training error is not a forecast test.

questions.q: Which models belong to the time-series foundation-model family? (pick all)
why: Holt-Winters is a classical method fitted per series.

questions.q: Scenario: your forecasts need promotion and price information that is known in advance. A zero-shot target-only model scores well on a plain-history test. What do you do?
options: Test whether a model with covariates (global GBM) does better, and consider combining both
why: It cannot use the promotion information.
Correct: covariates often matter a lot in retail.
One series gives too little data to tune.
